clue.text: Rich man goes under

definitions.meaning: The traditional name of the rich man in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus
sinks or plunges beneath the surface

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is ruined and goes under.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives is the Latin word for the wealthy figure in Luke's parable; plunging into water is also diving.

clue.text: Dentists may bring playtime to an end

definitions.meaning: a dentist may pull out the broken remains of teeth
in cricket the umpires end the day's play by pulling up the wicket posts

explanation.surface: A dentist's appointment cuts short a child's playtime.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the stumps are the three upright posts of the wicket; removing them ends the day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumps are both remnants of broken teeth, which dentists extract, and cricket's wicket posts, pulled at close of play.

clue.text: Article in box lifted into vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
the article goes inside the word for the box

parts.note: the box is slang for television, TV
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something is taken out of a box and put into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside TV to make TAV, and 'lifted' turns that upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large tank or tub for holding liquids, a kind of container.

clue.text: Cross about American vessel

indicators.note: the word for cross goes around the abbreviation for American

parts.note: to span a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about an American ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in East Asia.

clue.text: K as 1000 I put so incorrectly?

indicators.note: the letters put down wrongly are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether writing K for a thousand is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: K seems to be the thousand abbreviation (as in 10K), but it is the chemical symbol. 'incorrectly' rearranges AS, M and IPUTSO.
explanation.definitionFit: K is the chemical symbol of the alkali metal element with atomic number 19.

clue.text: Old wine, one imbibed by friend? It's possible

indicators.note: drunk by the friend, so these pieces sit inside the word for friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A friend drinks some vintage wine, and maybe that is possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent, a dark red Spanish wine, is rare outside crosswords; 'imbibed by' sets the old wine and one inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Something potential is latent and capable of coming about, so it is possible.

clue.text: Belief in forgotten ethics

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words forgotten ethics

explanation.surface: Some principle lies buried in a set of morals no one remembers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held to be true.

clue.text: Succeeded on traditional lines — i.e. brought in army

indicators.note: the abbreviation i.e. is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
old means traditional, of long standing
RY is short for railway, a set of lines
taken as written without the stops

explanation.surface: A conventional general hands over to his successor and the army is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: S for succeeded comes from family trees; the railway lines are RY. 'brought in' sets the i.e. between the traditional and the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery means soldiers collectively, a body of troops.

clue.text: Supervisor of those working on paper

definitions.text: Supervisor of those working on paper

parts.words: Supervisor of those working on paper
parts.note: the people working on paper are candidates sitting a written exam, watched over by an official

explanation.surface: Someone oversees office staff doing paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a clerical manager; the 'paper' is an exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam hall supervisor watches candidates to prevent cheating.

clue.text: Spot a suitable victim

definitions.meaning: an easy target for a swindler

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a likely victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a blemish, and a con artist's dupe is an easy target, both called by this word.

clue.text: Gold fruit gathered by new person operating mechanically

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Gold and fruit are collected by a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot-like individual acting without thought behaves like a machine.

clue.text: About to have a good time in bar

indicators.note: about tells us to turn round the word that follows

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate and enjoy oneself

explanation.surface: Someone is about to enjoy themselves in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the point of', but it reverses REVEL. The bar is a crowbar, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid rod used to prise things, a crowbar.

clue.text: Batsman getting a duck had to be ruthless

definitions.text: Batsman getting a duck had to
definitions.meaning: in cricket a duck is a score of zero, so the batsman's innings ends with nothing
to be willing to do anything, however bad, to get one's way

explanation.surface: A batsman out without scoring had to be merciless.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is an innings of no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone with no scruples who will do anything to win.

clue.text: Past one's peak, both literally and metaphorically

definitions.text: Past one's peak, both literally and metaphorically

parts.words: Past one's peak, both literally and metaphorically
parts.note: having gone beyond a summit on a walk, and also being too old to be at one's best

explanation.surface: Someone has crossed the summit and is also past it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means too old to be effective, and literally beyond the top of a rise.

clue.text: Underfunded person easily defeated in argument

definitions.meaning: someone with no real money or substance behind them
a feeble position set up only to be knocked down

explanation.surface: A poor man loses every debate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both someone without financial backing and a weak opponent or position set up to be refuted.

clue.text: Addict's continued enjoyment of legal right

definitions.meaning: in law, the continued exercise of a right that establishes it

explanation.surface: A drug taker keeps enjoying his legal entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal sense is obscure: 'user' is the continued use of a right, such as a footpath, over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug taker is a user, and in law user means the exercise of a right over time.

clue.text: Despised, neglected heroine recalled in novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A scorned, overlooked heroine is remembered in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals the anagram of RECALLEDIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine was scorned and neglected by her stepfamily before meeting the prince.

clue.text: After a number of years, new church goes into decline

parts.note: a decade is ten years
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: After some years, a new church falls into decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral or cultural decline or decay.

clue.text: Thin cake — fellow mostly gobbled it up

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: gobbled means ate

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man wolfs down most of a thin cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ATE to AT; 'up' turns IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is a flat unleavened Indian bread, a thin round griddle cake.

clue.text: Bowl last ball in dark

parts.note: in cricket, to pitch is to bowl the ball
in snooker the black is the final ball potted

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler sends down the final ball of the day as light fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last ball' looks like cricket, but it is snooker, where the black is potted last.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally without light means utterly dark.

clue.text: Essential oil for Bismarck

definitions.meaning: attar, a fragrant oil from rose petals
the first name of the German chancellor von Bismarck

explanation.surface: Bismarck is offered some essential oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a variant of attar of roses, and Prince Otto von Bismarck was Germany's Iron Chancellor.

clue.text: For climbs you need balance

explanation.surface: Climbers need good balance.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend a wall is to scale it, and a weighing balance is a pair of scales.

clue.text: Coppers stride out, exhibiting pride in their force

indicators.note: out means the letters are out of their proper order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Police officers march out showing pride in their force.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means the morale and loyalty shared by members of a group.

clue.text: No time for paper to come out

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: tissue is thin soft paper

explanation.surface: There is no time for a newspaper to be published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' suggests a newspaper, but it is TISSUE paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to emerge or flow out.

clue.text: Fancy man supporting wife

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece holds up the first, so it goes below

parts.note: him is a man

explanation.surface: A fancy man supports his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy man' is a lover, but Fancy is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a passing impulse or caprice.

clue.text: One amongst many in a group of flags

indicators.note: amongst places the one letter inside the word for many

parts.note: a host is a large number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One flag flies among many in a display.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoist is a set of signal flags raised together.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval signal made of several flags flown together is called a hoist.

clue.text: Jerusalem artichoke, for example, making child' meal, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said aloud

parts.note: a child is a son, and meal is ground grain, flour

explanation.surface: A Jerusalem artichoke makes a meal for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem artichoke is a species of Helianthus, the genus that bears large yellow flowers.

clue.text: Leaders of Western Alliance rejected military action

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Western powers reject armed conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between nations is war.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly I'll impede only one bit moved forward

indicators.note: a single letter of the phrase is shifted towards the front

explanation.surface: A bug declares it will get in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In ILLIMPEDE the M moves to the front to give the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-legged arthropod is a typical creepy-crawly.

clue.text: Xanthippe not totally cunning

indicators.note: the word is not complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: shrewd means sharp and cunning

explanation.surface: Socrates' wife is not quite clever.
explanation.walkthrough: Xanthippe, wife of Socrates, was proverbially a scold.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates' wife is the classic example of a nagging, bad-tempered woman.
